title: The conormal module of a standard smooth presentation is free on the equations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge c\ge0$ integers, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P$, $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq P$ and $S=P/I$, and assume that $S$ with the identity is a standard smooth presentation [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], i.e. the image in $S$ of $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{1\le i,j\le c}$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] is a unit of $S$. Then the conormal module $I/I^2$, an $S$-module, is a free $S$-module with basis the classes $f_1\bmod I^2,\dots,f_c\bmod I^2$; in particular $I/I^2\cong S^c$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00T7 (label lemma-standard-smooth, line 37274), part (3) and the first paragraph of its proof (the classes of the f_i map to a basis of the first c summands of the naive cotangent complex)
